pros: Captures tachometer rotation speed (contextual info for normalization)
No data is discarded; model decides what to use
Current trained models use this config — backward compatible
cons: Tachometer may add noise/redundancy for fault type classification

pros: Removes tachometer (primarily rotation-speed signal, low fault discrimination)
Cleaner input for fault frequency analysis
Simpler FPGA input path (fewer ADC channels needed)
cons: Loses microphone channel (has moderate discriminativity — see scores)
Breaks backward compatibility with current models
Requires retraining and updating EXPECTED_NUM_COLUMNS in config

forward_pass_test: 8-channel: input (8, 1024, 8) -> output (8, 4) OK. 6-channel: input (8, 1024, 6) -> output (8, 4) OK.
implementation_note: To switch between configs, add CHANNEL_SELECTION to src/config.py and update prepare_dataset.py to apply column slicing (e.g., values = values[:, ACTIVE_CHANNEL_INDICES]). Also update EXPECTED_NUM_COLUMNS and retrain the model. The Transformer architecture only requires updating the input_projection layer size; d_model, n_heads, and depth are unchanged.
